description:
From the fz-k22.21 investigation (2026-07-15). A strengthened in-process double-compile check (two independent Compiler2/World/Types instances compiling fixtures2/behavior/enum_predicate_search.fz) proves the published BackendProgram's executable inventory (function, need) is stable across runs, but full struct equality still fails: the type interner (types/mod.rs::TypeInterner::intern, arena insertion order = raw u32 id) mints a small cluster of fresh types in a different relative order between the two runs. Traced with an intern-call trace (each fresh Descr logged via its canonical Types::display rendering, not raw id) to a narrow, reproducible window: the reduce_while continuation/predicate-closure construction for closures #66/#70/#74/#76/#78/#82/#84/#87/#88 (the fixture's search/take/drop predicate lambdas) always interns in run-A order XOR run-B order, a pure permutation of the same content (never missing/extra entries -- verified via an executable-inventory fingerprint that matches exactly).

This is NOT either of the two circular tie-breaks fz-k22.21 closed (ground_surface_for_template_in_session -- already deleted in fz-k22.23; ContributionMap::apply's Debug-text sort -- fixed to use semantic::StableSortKey/Types::display). It is a new, unaudited source introduced by fz-k22.23's callable-flow actual-use closure (the 'disposable production-shaped loop' that enumerates each member's CallableFlowFact direct_edges/first_class_edges and unions owner->resolution edges), which post-dates and was not covered by the original fz-k22.13/eae19c725 determinism-pinning audit.

Suspected mechanism: some fold over a HashMap/HashSet of candidate closures/targets in jobs/runtime_demand.rs (derive_callable_flow_facts_for_executable_product and neighbors -- callable_flow_edges_for_targets, callable_flow_resolution_edges_product, ground_dispatch_surfaces) decides the order union()/arrow() mint fresh combination types, OR a downstream BTreeSet<CallableSurface>/BTreeSet<CallableTarget> (semantic.rs) whose Ord is itself Ty-value-dependent inherits and amplifies an earlier divergence once any upstream Ty numbering differs (a cascading effect observed directly: fixing one confirmed HashMap iteration hazard in derive_callable_flow_facts_for_executable_product, local_callable_producers, changed which cluster diverged but did not eliminate the divergence).

Confirmed NOT a correctness or CLI-observable-output issue at current HEAD: fz2 run fixtures2/behavior/enum_predicate_search.fz stays byte-identical across 10+ repeats, and the JIT-outcome equality test (compiling_the_same_root_twice_through_the_jit_reaches_the_same_outcome) passes. The gap is specifically that raw BackendProgram struct equality (Ty id level) is not yet provable, so any FUTURE consumer that keys off raw Ty order (a new sort, a new Debug-derived hash, a new golden-file byte comparison) is at risk of inheriting this exact hazard.

Investigate: instrument TypeInterner::intern with a temporary trace (as done for this investigation) to log each fresh Descr via Types::display; diff two runs' logs after stripping the leading id to find the first content-identical-but-reordered cluster; audit every unordered (HashMap/HashSet) iteration in jobs/runtime_demand.rs reachable from derive_callable_flow_facts_for_executable_product before that point; sort by a ValueId/FunctionId-derived key (never a Ty-derived key) at the fold site, following the same idiom as eae19c725 and fz-k22.21's local_callable_producers fix.
title: fz-k22: residual Ty interning-order divergence in the k22.23 callable-flow actual-use closure
